I have written some notes on how to hook up Kate with a new LSP server that I am developing and using:

https://lean.castedo.com/kate/

My quick impression is there are some issues using lake serve with Kate that are solved by using lspleank lake. I've chosen to document Kate in part due to @Hagb (Junyu Guo) sharing
his KDE Syntax Highlighting XML file; thank you!

I use Vim 9, but I am minimizing how many editor specific tweaks I develop and maximising how many standard LSP cross-editor functionality I can code into this new LSP server lspleank (and webleank). I hope these LSP server enhancements transfer to Kate and many other editors.

I suspect @Kevin Cheung, @Bulhwi Cha, and @Malvin Gattinger are Kate users. If you have any feedback, additional tips/suggestions/links/knowledge to share for the above documentation please let me know. This includes any info for Kate uses to use alternative methods to using LSP for Lean with Kate.

Early adopter pain feedback from Kate (or Vim 9) users is appreciated.

Cool stuff, but I don't really use Kate. (I was mostly involved in the other thread because I cared about the pandoc lean syntax file which was based on the one that kate uses. But I am not even sure what became of that.)

I tried lspleank in Kate and after a few minutes of use, it seems to work pretty well. Using the Kate diagnostics panel to implement the infoview is pretty clever, although is there some way to move the diagnostics panel to the right side instead of bottom?
Whatever cleverness you see in the diagnostics panel is not cleverness by me. I don't have lspleank doing anything with those LSP messages, they are straight from the lake serve.

For now, i'm trying to minimize doing anything editor-specific and more inclined to see what can be pulled off with webleank and a "Lean editor sidekick". More info at lean.castedo.com/webleank and an example sidekick is p.lean.castedo.com, but warning it's currently only for the adventerous! :wink:
So far I see p.lean.castedo.com working with Kate BTW. But this sidekick is obviously not very polished right now. It's a proof-of-concept mainly, but I hope to make something i'm happy to use.

FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'lake'

lake is in the /home/chabulhwi/.elan/bin/ subdirectory.

This is almost certainly due to ~/.elan/bin not being in the PATH environment variable when kate is started. Here's a quick fix for now: edit the command in ~/.config/kate/lspclient/settings.json to be the following

{
    "servers": {
        "lean": {
            "command": ["lspleank", "stdio", "--", "/home/chabulhwi/.elan/bin/lake", "serve"],
...
Starting kate from the command line in a shell session that has the PATH set to include ~/.elan/bin might also be a quick work around.

Based on the above, for lspleank v0.4 I plan to make the following fixes/enhancements:
https://gitlab.com/castedo/lspleanklib/-/work_items/2
https://gitlab.com/castedo/lspleanklib/-/work_items/1
Thanks for the feedback!

As a minor good-to-know, the command

lspleank lake

is a shortcut to

lspleank stdio -- lake serve

and what follows the -- is whatever command is to be run to launch a Lake LSP server.
A CLI reference available at https://gitlab.com/castedo/lspleanklib/-/blob/main/README.md and https://github.com/castedo/lspleanklib/blob/main/README.md

[11:53:57 ￼ LSP Client Log] Started server lean@/home/chabulhwi: /home/chabulhwi/.local/bin/lspleank stdio -- /home/chabulhwi/.elan/bin/lake serve
[11:53:57 ￼ LSP Server Log] lean@/home/chabulhwi
error: [root]: no configuration file with a supported extension:
/home/chabulhwi/lakefile.lean
/home/chabulhwi/lakefile.toml
warning: package configuration has errors, falling back to plain `lean --server`

On Kate, I opened the folder /home/chabulhwi/lean-projects/lean-playground, but the LSP server attempted to find the lakefile.toml file in my home directory.
Despite this, the server appears to be working fine.

In this case, lspleank is doing something clever, something I first noticed @Julian Berman 's lean.nvim plugin doing ... which is launching multiple lake serve subprocesses. So that error message is actually from the first lake serve subprocess and what is working fine is due to a second lake serve process that lspleank has launched.

I suspect for Kate users lspleank is useful because "workspace" in Kate is $HOME and this is incompatible with what "workspace" means to lake, but lspleank providing the language intelligence that lake is not.
... namely the intelligence to search for Lake workspace directories rather than expecting the editor to have the same defintion of "workspace" as Lake
